note: VOA news package on US shipbuilding (standard licence: url and time only, no frames committed), 0:00-2:30: b-roll between interviews. Labelled by eye from a 1 fps contact sheet of 0-150 s and frames with a 0.1-width grid. Subject shots: a submarine's wake crossing a fleet at sea (0-4.9 s, moving right from x 0.33 to 0.50), a worker on an orange lift against a hull (41.8-44.2 s, x 0.45), a worker at a machine on the right of a factory floor (126-129.2 s, x 0.80, profile face in 58% of frames). Must stay whole: the bar-chart animation (64.3-70.9 s, text and growing bars), a sailor waving a flag at the bow's tip of a docked ship (59.5-61.4 s: the ship is the subject, the moving flag is at the frame's edge) and a wide dockside carrier (44.2-46.7 s, motion spread). The other shots (interviews, factory b-roll with diffuse motion) are not labelled. Fails since the switch to YuNet (2026-11), a finding, not a label problem: YuNet boxes the machine worker's profile face in every frame of 126-129.2 s (UltraFace in 58%), at 13% of the frame height, so the shot is no longer face-free and the small-face rule makes it a corner stack before the subject crop is considered; the subject and keep-whole windows elsewhere all agree.
